tasks.short: Present an authorised position in arbitration or labour negotiations and record the outcome.

steps.what: Retrieve the agreement, case chronology, correspondence and relevant employee records.
Prepare the position brief, supporting evidence and anticipated questions.

loop.input: Approved evidence bundle, research brief and negotiation mandate.
loop.output: Position brief with source references and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check references against source passages; specialist checks arguments, omissions and mandate limits.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per brief; unsupported points remain flagged for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case narratives and arguments vary; templates handle structure but cannot compose the substantive position.

steps.what: Agree the position, settlement limits and escalation points.
Present arguments, answer challenges and negotiate within the approved mandate.
Write the outcome record and identify commitments needing further approval.

loop.input: Specialist's hearing notes, provisional outcome and approved mandate.
loop.output: Draft outcome record, attributed commitments and unresolved approval requests.
loop.check: Specialist checks every commitment against notes; mandate checks flag departures without authorising them.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes use varied wording and contain conditional or disputed commitments.

steps.what: File the reviewed record and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: An access-controlled integration assembles evidence from {HCM}, {EMAIL} and {DOCS}; bounded drafting loops prepare referenced briefs and outcome records. The specialist conducts the hearing, while {WORKFLOW} routes commitments outside the approved mandate to the HR manager and creates approved follow-up tasks in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits in separate records, and case-specific arguments need substantial editing. Bargaining authority cannot be reduced to a document template.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing access controls, document templates and workflow tools support the structure. AI-assisted coding can reduce integration effort, while bounded drafting handles variable narratives.
tasks.still_hard: Contested facts, changing positions and settlement authority remain difficult. GDPR protection of sensitive employee data and applicable national rules need case-specific attention.
tasks.human_edge: Credibility, listening, persuasive advocacy and knowing when a concession will damage trust.

ambition.what: Pre-hearing challenge rehearsal for line managers.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling files and more time rehearsing arguments and resolving disputes. Settlement rights stay within the existing mandate; no additional binding authority is assumed.

reach.learn: Budget limits, escalation thresholds and who can bind the employer.

reach.task: Review disputed treatment for discrimination concerns.
reach.learn: Protected-ground analysis and how to present sensitive evidence fairly.

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly and action tracking can use deterministic integrations; bargaining remains human work.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where automated decisions have legal or similarly significant effects.
A documented report containing nonexistent sources supports checking every generated reference.

assumptions: The specialist represents one side under an explicit mandate.
Time shares describe a typical contested case, including preparation and follow-up.
Human advocacy dominates, consistent with the priors; document preparation still offers meaningful savings.
Build estimates cover a pilot using existing systems, excluding procurement and unresolved legal disputes.
Access and consultation estimates include employee or works-council consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which side the specialist represents and who authorises binding commitments.
Whether records have stable case identifiers and accessible interfaces.
Which national rules and collective agreements apply.
The lawful basis and special-category condition for processing case data.
Whether hearing notes may be used for assisted drafting.
research_questions: Can every brief assertion be traced to a permitted source passage?
Which existing approval features can enforce settlement limits without custom code?
new_work: Review generated arguments and attributed commitments.
Resolve missing evidence and conflicting case records.
Maintain mandate templates, access rules and integrations.
Obtain separate approval for commitments outside the mandate.

tasks.short: Develop and assess workable alternatives to proposals raised in labour negotiations.

steps.what: Read the proposal against the current agreement and identify requested changes.

loop.output: Clause comparison with requested changes and missing details.
loop.check: Link changes to exact passages; specialist checks exceptions, definitions and omissions.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; unmatched clauses remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals often describe changes indirectly and use different wording from the agreement.

steps.what: Clarify interests, constraints and acceptable trade-offs with the relevant representatives.
Calculate costs and affected employee groups for candidate alternatives.
Develop alternative packages and describe their practical trade-offs.

loop.input: Reviewed constraints, verified cost scenarios and sourced legal research.
loop.output: Alternative packages with explicit trade-offs and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Use calculated costs unchanged; specialist checks feasibility, legal concerns and alignment with stated interests.
loop.stop: At most three packages and one correction pass; infeasible options are discarded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining interests into usable packages needs variable prose and contextual reasoning beyond a scenario calculator.

steps.what: Select the recommended package and authorise its use in negotiations.
Assemble the approved options brief for the negotiating team.

tasks.design: A deterministic scenario calculator uses authorised data from {HCM} and {PAYROLL} to compare costs and employee groups. Bounded loops compare proposal text and draft alternatives in {DOCS}; human discussions establish interests, and {WORKFLOW} records the HR manager's approval before producing the negotiating brief.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost models and proposal documents are disconnected. Acceptable trade-offs depend on relationships and interests that are rarely written down.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation rules and document assembly are established technology. Bounded extraction and drafting can connect varied proposals to those tools with less custom development.
tasks.still_hard: Affordability does not establish acceptability. Distributional effects, national employment rules and representatives' willingness to compromise remain judgement calls.
tasks.human_edge: Finding an exchange that both sides can defend to their constituents.

ambition.what: Reassess costed bargaining packages between negotiation rounds.

tasks.altitude: The specialist can bring several checked packages to each round and spend more time testing their acceptability. Approval of employer commitments remains with the authorised decision maker.

reach.task: Assess the distributional effect of a proposed pay settlement.
reach.learn: Pay components, workforce segmentation and recurring versus one-off costs.

reach.task: Check whether proposed pay rules can be implemented.
reach.learn: Effective dates, payroll cut-offs and exceptions in pay calculations.

evidence.claim: Scenario costing can use deterministic calculations; package acceptability requires human judgement.
GDPR Article 22 matters if the design extends into solely automated decisions significantly affecting employees.
AI systems intended for specified worker evaluation or employment decisions may fall within Annex III.

assumptions: The specialist develops employer-side alternatives with support from compensation staff.
A spreadsheet commonly joins pay exports to bespoke bargaining assumptions.
The calculator compares aggregate packages and does not select individual employment outcomes.
The priors support substantial conversation and judgement; drafting gains do not replace these steps.
Build estimates include a pilot and applicable national consultation, but exclude procurement.
unknowns: Available pay data, data quality and authorised aggregation levels.
Existing costing models and which assumptions have been validated.
Whether union membership or other special-category data would be processed.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approval rights.
Which proposed benefits can be implemented in the current payroll configuration.
research_questions: Can existing calculation features cover the main proposal types?
How reliably do extracted changes preserve exceptions and eligibility conditions?
new_work: Validate scenario assumptions and reconcile calculation results.
Review drafted packages for feasibility and omitted employee groups.
Maintain pay rules and effective-date logic.
Reassess GDPR and EU AI Act obligations if the scope expands to individual decisions.

tasks.short: Draft and agree procedures governing collective bargaining with employer and employee representatives.

steps.what: Collect existing procedures, agreements and relevant legal guidance.
Agree drafting scope, representation, meeting rules and unresolved process questions.
Draft procedure clauses and mark departures from the existing text.

loop.input: Approved clause library, procedure requirements and current procedure.
loop.output: Procedure draft with changes, source references and open points.
loop.check: Check required sections and cross-references; specialist verifies meaning and flags unsupported clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes per version; unresolved clauses return to human discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreed requirements require contextual wording, although standard clauses and document structure remain deterministic.

steps.what: Discuss disputed clauses and agree revisions with employer and employee representatives.
Check the revised procedure against applicable law and existing agreements.
Approve the final wording through the agreed representative process.
Publish the approved procedure and archive superseded versions.

tasks.design: A versioned clause library in {DOCS} supplies standard wording, while a bounded loop drafts only from agreed requirements and approved sources. {WORKFLOW} routes legal review and representative approval, then publishes the approved version in {DOCS} and sends an internal notice through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated drafting and version control sit around a process whose substance must be negotiated. Standard templates cover only part of the wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Document versioning and approval routing already exist. Bounded drafting can turn agreed requirements into a reviewable text without automating agreement between the parties.
tasks.still_hard: Representation rights, enforceability and ambiguous wording depend on national rules and the applicable agreements. A specialist cannot create government regulations merely by publishing a company procedure.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing a process that representatives regard as legitimate, especially when their interests conflict.

ambition.what: Joint procedure walkthrough for newly appointed employee representatives.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time managing versions and more time explaining disputed clauses and improving the bargaining process. Legal approval and representative authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Create an induction session on the agreed bargaining procedure.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, realistic exercises and checking procedural understanding.
Version control, effective dates and retention requirements.

evidence.claim: Clause assembly, version control and approval routing are established automation patterns.
Bargaining remains human work, with drafting open to bounded assistance.
In the Netherlands, specified HR data and monitoring arrangements require works-council consent.
A documented report failure supports verifying generated references before legal review.

assumptions: The typical employer drafts bargaining procedures rather than statutory regulations.
Employer and employee representatives retain their separate approval rights.
Time shares cover one drafting cycle; repeated negotiation rounds can increase the conversation share.
The priors favour drafting support, while the steps retain substantive consultation and legal review.
Build estimates cover a pilot and applicable employee consultation; bargaining delays are excluded.
unknowns: Which representative bodies and signatories must approve the procedure.
Applicable national rules and existing sector or company agreements.
Whether there is an approved clause library.
Which publication channels make the procedure authoritative.
Whether drafting materials contain personal or special-category data.
research_questions: Which clauses can be assembled unchanged from approved templates?
Can existing document approvals preserve each representative body's separate decision?
new_work: Review generated clauses and reconcile agreed revisions.
Maintain the approved clause library and legal source dates.
Resolve approval exceptions and conflicting versions.
Check that notices and training refer to the effective procedure.

tasks.short: Find relevant case law and previous hearing outcomes, then assess their applicability.

steps.what: Define the legal issue, relevant facts, jurisdiction and research scope.
Search a legal research database and the internal hearing register.
Retrieve decision texts, citation details and available appeal or status information.
Read decisions and compare facts, reasoning, outcomes and material differences.

loop.input: Retrieved decision texts, source metadata and scoped research question.
loop.output: Comparison of facts, reasoning and outcomes with exact source passages.
loop.check: Verify identifiers and quoted passages; specialist checks summaries, distinctions and missing context.
loop.stop: Process at most ten decisions per batch with one correction pass; incomplete texts require manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Facts and reasoning appear in varied prose; keyword search cannot produce a faithful comparison.

steps.what: Assess relevance, authority and uncertainty, then finalise the research brief.
Save the approved brief, source references and research date in the case file.

tasks.design: Configured searches in {OTHER}, the legal research database, retrieve decisions using specialist-approved criteria; a permitted integration stores source texts and metadata in {DOCS}. A bounded loop produces passage-linked comparisons, and the specialist assesses legal relevance before the approved research brief enters the case file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Search tools find documents, but specialists still read and compare lengthy decisions. Source access and inconsistent internal hearing records complicate retrieval.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search filters, document indexes and permitted retrieval interfaces handle discovery. Bounded text extraction can reduce reading and comparison work while retaining source checks.
tasks.still_hard: Completeness, appeal status and precedential weight vary by jurisdiction and source. Similar facts do not establish the same legal outcome.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising decisive factual differences and explaining uncertainty without overstating a precedent.

ambition.what: Early precedent check before a grievance escalates to a hearing.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time retrieving and summarising decisions and more time testing their relevance. The change supports earlier advice; it does not confer new authority to decide disputes.

reach.task: Research relevant decisions for a discrimination complaint.
reach.learn: Protected grounds, evidential standards and differences between factual similarity and legal authority.

reach.task: Prepare a sourced procedural briefing for a manager.
reach.learn: How to state the issue, qualify uncertainty and recognise when legal advice is needed.

evidence.claim: Search, retrieval and filing can be automated, while legal applicability requires human assessment.
A documented report containing nonexistent references demonstrates the need for source-grounded validation.
In the Netherlands, the cited mandatory DPIA list covers employee monitoring; this is relevant if research expands into monitoring.

assumptions: The employer has lawful access to a legal research database and an internal hearing archive.
Configured search supports the required jurisdiction and source filters.
Retrieval complies with source licensing and access restrictions.
Public decisions and confidential internal outcomes remain in separate access groups.
The automation prior is moderated: defining the issue and assessing applicability remain human.
Build estimates include access review and national consultation where applicable, excluding subscription procurement.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, languages and courts the research must cover.
Available source subscriptions, export rights and interfaces.
Completeness and confidentiality of internal hearing records.
Who must review legally consequential research conclusions.
Whether internal records require redaction or special-category processing safeguards.
research_questions: How does retrieval coverage compare with specialist searches on completed cases?
Which sources provide reliable appeal and subsequent-treatment information?
What review effort is needed to detect omitted decisive passages?
new_work: Verify source passages, citation identifiers and decision status.
Handle missing texts, licensing restrictions and poor scans.
Maintain search filters, source connectors and access separation.
Refresh briefs when relevant decisions or legal rules change.

role.altitude: The week shifts from file assembly, repeated drafting and document retrieval toward advocacy, package design and early dispute advice. Binding settlement, representative approval and legal decision rights remain with the existing authorised roles.
reach: Compensation and benefits managers: assess bargaining costs and distributional effects.
Equal opportunity representatives: connect dispute evidence to discrimination analysis.
Training and development specialists: teach agreed bargaining procedures.
Human resources specialists: provide earlier, sourced procedural guidance.
skills_to_grow: Frame research questions and verify legal sources.
Build and validate bargaining cost scenarios.
Review assisted drafts for omitted conditions and unsupported claims.
Apply GDPR access, retention and special-category safeguards.
Assess intended uses under the EU AI Act and applicable national rules.
Facilitate difficult conversations and negotiate defensible trade-offs.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early dispute advisory service combining verified precedent checks, costed settlement options and manager preparation, with human responsibility for advocacy and commitments.
